questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Both culture and academics were important to my choice. I chose unibo in part because they had some very exciting electives, including some that were not available at my home university. The reason I decided to go in the fall semester was also that the largest range of electives were available at this time.

More important than this however, is the fact that Bologna is a beautiful and historic city. Especially inside the old city walls, it is just old renaissance palaces, archways with terrazzo flooring, cozy plazas and a ton of gingko bilobas. Immideately to the south of the old city walls is also some potential very nice walks into more old architecture and nature. Bologna is also not a very large city, which makes it feel not to overwhelming. It is a very unique and beautiful city, with very nice people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn't super obvious. There was no information that you couldn't get, but you had to search a bunch of different places. You can setup these office visits with guides who are super helpful, but it's also kind of a hassle. In general, I think it was satisfactory, but it took way longer than necessary.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really a lot. Again, there are these helpdesk meetings you can setup, which you also need to do in order to "check in" at the university so you can get your student card. But like, the student card you gotta find out which campus near you has a student card vending machine, and then just go there and print it out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: While I think a lot could have been done to improve information for incoming students, and reply times are sometimes very slow, once you get a hold of someone, they are very helpful and polite.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It depends on how much you're willing to pay. Bologna is a small city with a large number of incoming exchange students. So the general price level of housing for incoming students is insane. Also, many landlords/ladys do not want to rent out their places for less than six months at a time, which is longer than most stays. I found my housing through something called saisa accommodation, which is the university's own matching service. I ended up renting a place from one of the professors of the uni.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Bologna is a small city. From most attractive places, you can walk to the campus and any social meetup spots. Transport in general in Bologna is very easy for able-bodied people. Even if you live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to have this online learning agreement to receive your erasmus grant. When it's approved you automatically get signed up to the final exams for the courses. Then you just gotta find the relevant courses in "virtuale" and sign up for them there too, and then you're pretty much done. Very easy, super simple, barely any work.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I mean the process of actually signing up for the courses was very simple, but again, getting the OLA in order took ages, because unibo had some very very long reply times.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted! A few of them were a bit crowded, but the lecturers are very flexible with moving rooms if necessary, and they are great at squeezing in all the exchange students they can manage.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Request a preliminary course catalogue from unibo as early as you can, and get a sense of which courses you would like to take. It can be a lot to dig through, but the search function is really helpful. Once the full course catalogue for your stay is released, start working on your OLA and having it approved as soon as possible, because, as mentioned, they can take very long to reply.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general I found the courses to be slightly lower level than the ones at my home uni. However there is much room to read extracurricular and additional materials, and the lecturers are happy to discuss their subjects of interests.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. One very nice thing though was that the classes were often smaller, and so there was a bit more time for each student. Also, there seems to be more of a culture of active participation in the classes, which is really nice, even if you don't feel comfortable participating to that degree yourself.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Behavioral Economics, Advanced Panel Data Methods, Information Economics, Machine Learning for Economists, Structural Macroeconometrics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I thought all of the courses were great. I would probably recommend the ones where you write a final project. The feedback you get is great and detailed, and you will often also get the opportunity to defend it with a presentation. It is a very good learning experience.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I thought there was gonna be a cheap public transportation card for all exchange students. However this was discontinued from the fall semester and onwards.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I knew housing was gonna be expensive, and it still turned out to be more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was unaware of any, except for one party for erasmus students. However, I think I might just not have been informed about them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you enjoy running I think the city is great for that :) Also the walk from Porta Saragozza to Basilica di San Luca is great.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can take a short trip to some of the nearby cities like Modena, or go a bit further and stay for a weekend in Milano or Firenze.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to adjust to the culture. One small challenge was that my italian isn't great, and many of the locals don't speak a lot of english. However they are eager to help you understand their italian and to understand your english.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students are super friendly and welcoming! Even if you're a bit shy, they'll take an interest in you and talk to you and make sure that you feel welcomed to the uni/class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There weren't really any that I found too challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Price of coffee and food in general. Also quality of coffee and food in general.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to start to take care of administrative stuff that unibo has to reply to/confirm early, because they can take very long to reply.

Start looking for housing early, potentially with other people, and maybe even with someone who is going in the semester after you, so you can get a good deal on a longer rental contract.

Go out to eat a lot. There are so many great and cozy places, and it is really not expensive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you don't want to spend a long time looking for expensive housing, check out the student hotel. A few of my friends stayed there. Very social and pretty close to campus, but also maybe a bit too social and like with party vibes every night.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was very fulfilling to experience that despite all of the things I was nervous about and the language barrier, I was still able to live a pretty comfortable life and like establish a routine in a completely different country. The challenges and mental hurdles I found out I was able to overcome.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Loneliness to be honest. Being so far away from friends and family and partner, and no matter how many friends you make at the host institution

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Via Saragozza, 3a, 40123 Bologna, 3rd Wave Espresso. Best coffee I have ever had, and I have had plenty. Really nice staff and regular costumers. Very local. The shop next door has a dog that sometimes slips out of the door and goes around and gets pets and scraps from the customers at 3rd wave.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
